transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My mind keeps jumping to every little thing around me, and I can’t stay focused on what I’m supposed to be doing anymore. It's making it incredibly hard to get my work done lately, so I figured I needed to talk to someone.
Have you struggled with these difficulties with focus and distractibility since you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

No, this is definitely a recent change for me, not something from when I was a kid. It really started ramping up about seven months ago when I transitioned from long-haul driving into a regional freight sales job. Since making that move, my focus has just completely fallen apart.

Beyond the difficulty focusing, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, or have you been feeling unusually worried and tense about your daily responsibilities?

No, I don't feel sad or lose interest at all—it's actually the opposite, and I've been feeling on top of the world and throwing myself into new woodworking and photography projects. I've read up on anxiety before, but right now I don't feel down, just incredibly wired and busy. I actually get really snapped and irritated if anyone tries to slow me down.

When you feel this 'wired' and energetic, do you ever feel like your thoughts are so fast that others can't keep up, or do you ever experience things—like hearing voices or seeing things—that others around you don't seem to notice?

Yes, absolutely—my thoughts race constantly and I talk a mile a minute, to the point where customers and family definitely struggle to keep up with my fast-shifting ideas. But as for hearing or seeing things that aren't there, no, I've never experienced anything like that.
Have you ever in your life experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or had a significant loss of interest in all your usual activities?
No, I haven't really experienced a period of persistent sadness or loss of interest like that. My main struggles have been with my mind racing and being way too active rather than feeling down.

During these periods where you feel wired, energetic, and your thoughts are racing, have you ever felt so out of control that you required hospitalization, or did these episodes cause such severe disruption that you were unable to function at work or maintain your personal safety?

No, I've never been hospitalized, but it has definitely caused some really severe disruptions in my life. I nearly lost a major sales account because of my poor follow-through, my boss has warned me about my erratic hours and overpromising, and my wife is furious that I'm missing family events and running up credit card debt on unfinished projects.
During these periods of being wired and energetic, have these symptoms lasted for at least one full week, or were they present for a shorter duration?

Oh, it's been much longer than just a week. These ups and downs with my mood, energy, and focus have been ramping up and causing real trouble for about seven months now. It has basically been a constant issue ever since I switched to this regional freight sales job.
Looking back at your life before these last seven months, have you ever experienced any other period of several days or weeks where you felt similarly high-energy, irritable, or unusually active?
No, I don't recall ever having periods like this before the last seven months. This level of high energy and irritability is completely new to me.

During these past seven months, have you ever felt so energetic and impulsive that you were completely unable to carry out your daily work or social responsibilities for several days at a time, or were you still able to maintain some level of functioning despite the disruptions?

I haven't been completely unable to work, but my functioning has been severely disrupted and I'm barely hanging on. I nearly lost a major client due to poor follow-through, my boss has warned me about my erratic hours, and my wife is furious because I'm missing family events and racking up credit card debt.

To clarify the intensity of these episodes, did your symptoms ever reach a point where you were completely unable to function at work or in your personal life for several days, or were you always able to maintain at least a basic level of functioning?

I was never completely bedridden or totally absent, but my functioning was highly chaotic and caused major damage. I nearly lost a major sales account because of my poor follow-through, got warnings from my boss about erratic hours and overpromising, and faced severe arguments at home for missing family events and running up credit card debt. It's not that I couldn't do anything, but rather that what I was doing was making a mess of my life.

Even if you haven't felt consistently sad for two weeks, have you ever experienced any distinct period in your life where you felt so low, hopeless, or lacked interest in everything that it was a noticeable departure from your usual self?
No, I've never experienced any periods like that where I felt extremely low, hopeless, or lost interest in things. My mood has never really dipped into feeling down or depressed like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a distinct period of elevated, expansive, and irritable mood accompanied by increased goal-directed activity, racing thoughts, and impulsivity (credit card debt, overpromising). These symptoms have lasted for seven months, causing significant social and occupational impairment, yet they do not meet the criteria for a full manic episode (no hospitalization, no psychosis, and the patient remained able to maintain basic, albeit chaotic, functioning).
